newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures in late rebound.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures in late rebound.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures see-sawed but still finished higher on Friday on late covering ahead of the three-day weekend.
Traders said prices were still shy of their day's ceilings on scale-up origin and trade sales.
New York's reversal from Thursday's dazzling rally had no real impact in London as the market did not really react when New York was up.
"There's no follow through here," said one. Another said: "They are two different markets, each pulling in a different direction."
London was called a hefty $100-$120 higher on numbers after Thursday's dazzling rally in New York. But it managed to gap just $29 at the open, basis July.
By the close, the benchmark contract was up $10 at $1,680 after an intraday high of $1,990. Its session low was $1,575.
The market is closed on Monday for a bank holiday, reopening on Tuesday.
Volume was a scant 3,383 lots, centred on July outrights and nearby spreads.
July/September was traded at $15 and May/July at $80.
London's July contract had been on an uphill struggle to get clear the $1,705 resistance due to large over-hanging producer sales.
A mini-rally in London on Thursday lured large Vietnamese and Indonesian sales.
On the demand side, roasters are well-stocked of robustas while funds would stay out unless July heads towards $1,720.

On the fundamental news, German roaster Tchibo Frisch-Roest Kaffee said on Friday it has raised its retail prices by up to one mark per 500 grams with immediate effect. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
